# Abscess incision and drainage

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Emergency medicine > Treatment approaches and procedures > Abscess incision and drainage*

[Original Article Link](/library/4F03R3)

---

## Summary

<u>Incision</u> and drainage (I&D) is a procedure used to drain <u>pus</u> from <u>skin</u> and <u>soft tissue</u> <u>abscesses</u>; it can be performed in both adults and children. This article describes bedside I&D, which should not be performed for <u>abscesses</u> that warrant surgical consultation such as those located near important structures (e.g., nerves, <u>arteries</u>) or in areas of cosmetic concern (e.g., face, <u>breast</u>). During the procedure, an <u>incision</u> is made into the overlying tissue to facilitate <u>pus</u> drainage. <u>Abscess irrigation</u> and packing may be performed after I&D, however, there is limited evidence to support their use. Complications include damage to surrounding structures and <u>abscess</u> recurrence.




For specific considerations regarding <u>abscesses</u> of the <u>Bartholin glands</u>, see “<u>Bartholin gland abscess</u>.”
